 FT: West Ham 4-1 Liverpool 
 Viviane Asseyi scored twice as West Ham gained their third Women's Super League victory of the season with a dominant home win over Liverpool.
 The Hammers started the day 12th in the table, having only scored five goals in seven league games, but they netted four times in the opening 62 minutes against the Reds.
 Asseyi grabbed the opener from the penalty spot in only the seventh minute after she had been fouled by Fuka Nagano to win the spot kick following good work down the left by Ines Belloumou.
 Leila Wandeler doubled the hosts' lead eight minutes later following a bright run and a one-two with Seraina Piubel before shooting past England international Khiara Keating.
 Asseyi hit the crossbar, but West Ham did not have to wait long to score again as Laia Codina made it 3-0 just before the break, although her 30-yard effort took a huge deflection off Jenna Clark before going in.
 It became 4-0 in the 62nd minute when Asseyi won a free-kick and she curled a superb effort just underneath the crossbar as Keating was beaten again.
 Liverpool pulled one back 10 minutes later with substitute Vivien Endemann's low shot taking a deflection off Codina to give the Reds a consolation goal.
 The victory took West Ham above Liverpool to 10th, with the Reds one point and one place below them in 11th.

 Guarino praises 'incredible' Asseyi published at 16:27 GMT 16:27 GMT 
 FT: West Ham 4-1 Liverpool 
 West Ham United 
 West Ham manager Rita Guarino said: "Very happy, very proud of the team, we deserved this win. From the first minute we played a very good game with pressure, with defending, attacking, the effort we put in this game. 
 "We were able to use the space we needed to create this type of opportunities so I'm very proud.
 "We need this kind of energy [against Manchester City next week] and it's not simple to go away in the house of the champions."
 On two-goal Viviane Asseyi: "She missed a hat-trick unfortunately but very happy. She is an incredible player so very happy for her and very happy in the way the team helped her to make this type of performance."

 'Unacceptable' published at 16:21 GMT 16:21 GMT 
 FT: West Ham 4-1 Liverpool 
 Liverpool 
 Liverpool manager Gareth Taylor said: "A flat start, we gave away a decisive penalty in the first five minutes and then you are always facing an uphill battle. 
 "They were very direct, we had a lot of play but we still need to do more with it in the final third as that scoreline should've looked closer.
 "They [West Ham] always seemed to come out with the ball, which is unacceptable from us.
 "Your initial feeling is frustration and disappointment and we have to dust ourselves down and get ready for a game at Anfield [against Arsenal] next week."

 'We all need to be better' published at 16:15 GMT 16:15 GMT 
 FT: West Ham 4-1 Liverpool 
 Liverpool 
 Liverpool captain Grace Fisk said: "We were way off it in a lot of departments, competing, small actions, duels, they were better than us. 
 "Disappointing as I feel performances have been really positive, even if results have not gone our way, but we were way off it it so a disappointing day.
 "They started well and we didn't, that happens in football but we never got to grasp the intensity of the game. We lack creativity at the moment and that has been a problem. 
 "They were really clinical and at half-time we were three-nil down. We came out believing but it did not happen. We all need to be better. I don't think anyone can hold their heads up this week. We will come back fighting for sure."

 'A really important win for us' published at 16:05 GMT 16:05 GMT 
 FT: West Ham 4-1 Liverpool 
 West Ham United 
 West Ham's two-goal scorer Viviane Asseyi said: "We work a lot in every training session and we give everything in every game. It's a collective win today and I'm really happy.
 "We know in this league every game is really hard to win and you have to be focused from the beginning to the end. Unfortunately we conceded a goal, but we won this game and it's a really important win for us.
 "This league is the best in the world at the moment. Manchester City [who they play on Saturday] is the best team in the league for me. We can enjoy this victory and next week we will be focused on Manchester City."
 On scoring a free-kick: "That's why I annoy the goalkeepers at the end of practice, for these kind of moments, so thanks to them."
